summaries.demographer: Balbir Kakarala is a 28-year-old never-married South Asian Indian American man living with one roommate in a rented apartment in Brooklyn, NY 11211 (Q11, Q51, Q84, Q89). He was born in New York City to immigrant parents from India, with Punjabi Sikh and Telugu family backgrounds, and he lived with both parents at age 16 (Q86-Q99). He has a bachelor's degree, works full time as a training and development specialist, and has stable salaried employment with benefits (Q65-Q78, Q90). He has no children, no spouse, and maintains close but non-cohabiting ties to his parents and a small friend network (Q05-Q07).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Balbir shows a mix of planning and present-biased spontaneity: he uses spreadsheets, task blocks, and structured work habits, but acknowledges relaxed financial habits around food, travel, and gear (Q03, Q56-Q62, Q83). He can absorb a $400 emergency and has savings, but Brooklyn rent, student loans, and career investments constrain his sense of security (Q61-Q64, Q82-Q83). His choices are motivated by usefulness, identity, and skill growth: he chose instructional design because translating complex material felt meaningful and plans to pursue CPLP for advancement (Q02, Q65, Q108). Peer and community influence appear in running-club accountability, voting behavior, and board-game social routines (Q07, Q15, Q23, Q32).
summaries.political_scientist: Balbir is a regular voter who identifies as a moderately to strongly Democratic, progressive-leaning pragmatist (Q23-Q25, Q95-Q96). His issue priorities include housing affordability, transit, education, health care, climate, immigrant rights, racial justice, and competent implementation (Q24-Q25). He was significantly affected by Black Lives Matter, attended one march, donated occasionally, and discusses race and anti-Blackness with friends and family (Q26-Q30). His civic orientation is participatory but measured, combining voting, tutoring, local awareness, and selective activism rather than full-time organizing (Q17, Q23, Q29).
summaries.psychologist: Balbir presents as reflective, conscientious, analytical, and relationally steady, with a preference for structure but some tolerance for spontaneity and iteration (Q01-Q04, Q15-Q18). He reports anxiety around work expectations, financial uncertainty, and future planning, but not diagnosed depression; coping strategies include running, meditation, cooking, task lists, and talking with trusted people (Q43-Q45, Q50). His self-concept centers on clarity, usefulness, family, learning, and cultural groundedness (Q02, Q65, Q109). He maintains a small close social network and balances solitary restoration with recurring group activities such as board games, tutoring, and running (Q07, Q17, Q43).
